canonical_statement: The study cannot rule out unmeasured confounding despite extensive measured-confounder adjustment and sensitivity analyses.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: Some laboratory variables had substantial missingness, including eGFR and UACR, and the multiple-imputation analysis assumes the missingness could be predicted by included covariates.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: The SCREAM data lacked left ventricular ejection fraction, so the study could not distinguish HFpEF from HFrEF or estimate subtype-specific effects.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: Treatment discontinuation rates were high, which can bias intention-to-treat estimates toward the null and motivated the per-protocol analysis.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: The cohort represents Stockholm and may not generalize to settings with different care patterns or baseline HHF incidence; differences in baseline risk also change absolute treatment benefit.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: Race and ethnicity data were unavailable because such collection is prohibited in Sweden by law.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: The study could not calculate PREVENT-HF because key variables including smoking status, BMI, and blood pressure were unavailable.

source_anchor.paragraph: Strengths and Weaknesses of the Study

canonical_statement: The authors stated that the main findings require replication in future high-quality studies and noted that relatively few participants had heart failure at baseline.
The study data are not publicly available but may be shared on reasonable request to Juan-Jesus Carrero.
The deidentified-data study was deemed not to require informed consent and was approved by the regional ethical review boards and the Swedish National Board of Welfare (2017/793-31).
The study reports grant support for Xu, Tuttle, Carrero and the SCREAM project, and Fu from Chinese, US, Swedish, Dutch, Karolinska, and Leiden funding sources.
The authors state that the funders had no role in study design or conduct, data collection or analysis, manuscript preparation or review, or the decision to submit.

Katherine R. Tuttle disclosed investigator-initiated grants, consultancy and speaker fees, data-safety-monitoring-board roles, and professional leadership roles; the other authors reported no conflicts.
